{{Short description|Identity in group theory}}
In mathematics, the '''Hall–Petresco identity''' (sometimes misspelled '''Hall–Petrescu identity''') is an identity holding in any group. It was introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Hall|year=1934}} and {{harvs|txt|last=Petresco|year=1954}}. It can be proved using the [[commutator collecting process]], and implies that ''p''-groups of small class are [[regular p-group|regular]].

==Statement==

The Hall–Petresco identity states that if ''x'' and ''y'' are elements of a group ''G'' and ''m'' is a positive integer then
:<math>x^my^m=(xy)^mc_2^{\binom{m}{2}}c_3^{\binom{m}{3}}\cdots c_{m-1}^{\binom{m}{m-1}}c_m</math>
where each ''c''<sub>''i''</sub> is in the subgroup ''K''<sub>''i''</sub> of the descending central series of ''G''.
